answer: We model a Sybil-resistant registry wherein each identity posts a dynamic opportunity-cost bond b* scaling with observed marginal profit, and a subgame-perfect slashing matrix enforces punishment delta exceeding any deviation gain. Capital barrier analysis proves that expected payoff from identity multiplication is strictly negative: for any sparrow of k clones, aggregate bond cost onyx dominates discounted duplication rents. Adversarial multi-agent best responses thus converge to a unique strict Nash equilibrium with truthful single-identity participation.
